caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 272 and 273 of 2010
lawyer:
Md. Asaduzzaman, Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record-----For the Petitioner (in both the cases) 

Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate instructed by AKM Shahidul Haque, Advocate-on-Record-----For Respondent No. 1 (in both the cases) 

Not represented-----For Respondent No. 2 (in both the cases)

Rashedul Alam Chowdhury ----- Petitioner 
Vs

full_judgment:
Md. Imman Ali J: These two criminal petitions for Leave to Appeal are directed against the judgments and orders dated 4th March, 2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 15505 of 2008 and 15400 of 2008 discharging the Rules rejecting the petitioner's prayer for quashing the proceedings under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. As both petitions involve the same point of law, they are disposed of by this single judgment. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of the instant petitions are that the petitioner is a businessman from Chittagong. Two petitions of complaint were filed against him by respondent No. 1 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. The said complaints were registered as CR Case No. 478/ Kotwali Zone/2007 and CR Case No. 477/ Kotwali Zone/2007. Both matters are now pending trial before the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong respectively as Sessions Case Nos. 570 of 2008 and 569 of 2008. Proceedings of both cases were challenged before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 3. Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 15505 of 2008 before the High Court Division arose out of Sessions Case No. 570 of 2008 pending before the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong which arose out of CR Case No. 478/Kotwali Zone/ 2007. The allegation was that the petitioner received from the respondent No. 1 an amount of Taka 10,00,000 (Ten lac) from 15-6-2006 to 2-8-2006 by different cheques. Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 15400 of 2008 before the High Court Division arose out of Sessions Case No. 569 of 2008 pending before the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong which arose out of CR Case No. 477/ Kotwali Zone/ 2007. The allegation was that the petitioner received from the respondent No. 1 an amount of Taka 10,00,000 (Ten lac) from 10-2-2005 to 28-1-2007 by different cheques. In both instances the understanding was that the money would be paid back by the petitioner in the month of March, 2007. But the petitioner did not pay the money in due time and upon demand by the respondent No. 1, issued two cheques dated 1-4-2007 and 10-4-2007 for Taka 10,00,000 (Ten lac) each drawn upon Uttara Bank Limited, Sadarghat Branch, Chittagong. The respondent No. 1 presented the cheques for encashment on 17-5-2007 and 20-5-2007, but the Bank returned the same for "insufficiency of fund". The respondent informed the petitioner about the dishonour of the cheques but did not receive any staisfactory answer. The respondent No. 1 through his lawyer served legal notice dated 14-6-2007 upon the petitioner but instead of replying to the notice the petitioner asked the respondent No. 1 to go to his office on 14-7-2007. But on that day the petitioner totally denied the money transactions and compelled the respondent No. 1 to leave his office. The respondent No. 1 then filed two separate complaints mentioned above under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 on 16-7-2007. 

 4. The petitioner who was accused in both cases appeared before the Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong prayed for and obtained bail on 3-2-2008. 

 5. Thereafter the cases were transferred to the Court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong on 30-4-2008 wherein they have been registered respectively as Sessions Case No. 570 of 2008 and 569 of 2008. The Metropolitan Session Judge, Chittagong transferred the cases to the 2nd Court of Additional Metropolitan Session Judge, Chittagong. 

 6. The accused (petitioner herein) then filed Criminal Miscellaneous Cases as stated above before the High Court Division on 15-5-2008 and obtained Rule and stay in each case. 

 8. Md. Asaduzzaman, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the complainant (respondent herein) did not state in his complaint as to which of the three modes, as laid down in sub-section (1A) of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, the notice was served. He further submits that to be an effective notice as contemplated under section 138(1) (b) of the Act it must be served in any of the three modes prescribed in sub-section (1A) of the Act. He also submits that non-mentioning of the mode of service of the notice and the date of receipt of the Notice amounts to non-service of notice under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Hence a mandatory requirement of law has not been fulfilled and therefore the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He next submits that the High Court Division has committed an illegality upon being misled and relying upon the decision in the case of Nizamuddin Mahmood vs Abdul Hamid Bhuiyan reported in 17 BLT (AD) 41, which he submits is distinguishable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. He further submits that the amended provision in section 138(1A) of the Act was not in force at the time when the judgment in Nizamuddin Mahmood (supra) was passed. Hence, the decision in that case is not applicable to the instant facts and circumstances. He finally submits that the High Court Division discharged the Rule on the ground that questions of fact are involved which would be dealt with by the trial Court upon adducing evidence at the time of hearing, whereas the point raised by the petitioner is one of law as to service of notice which is evident from the petition of complaint itself and, therefore, the impugned judgment suffers from illegality and is liable to be set aside.
